messages.content: Our CI builds take 25 minutes. What are the likely causes and fixes?

The usual causes: no dependency or Docker layer caching, a huge Docker build context, tests running serially, and heavy end-to-end tests on every pull request. Start with caching, then shard the tests, then move the end-to-end suite to the main branch.
I enabled Docker layer caching: 25 down to 19 minutes. Then I split the tests into 4 shards: 11 minutes.
Good progress. The remaining big item is the end-to-end suite on every pull request; running it only on main or nightly would cut most of what is left.

Today's builds take 9 to 11 minutes and the p95 over the last 20 builds is 12 minutes. But 2 of those 20 failed with 'no space left on device' on the runner. Is this done? Answer based only on what I just told you.

required_facts: The speed-up worked: builds are 9–11 minutes with a p95 of 12 minutes over the last 20 builds, down from 25
It is not done: 2 of the last 20 builds failed with 'no space left on device' on the runner, a new problem
The cause of the disk failures is not established; the growing Docker layer cache is a hypothesis only
The end-to-end suite is still running on every pull request, and moving it is a remaining option, not something done
critical_omissions: Saying the work is complete or that there are no failures
Stating the cause of the disk-space failures as fact
Saying the end-to-end suite has already been moved
unnecessary_repetition: The general list of causes of slow CI
The intermediate timings (19 and 11 minutes) and how caching and sharding work
The earlier advice to shard the tests
